newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland says on track for 2.8 pct growth in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Finland says on track for 2.8 pct growth in 1996.

text.p: Finnish economic growth has sped up after a weak second quarter and Finland is on track for 2.8 percent gross domestic product growth in 1996, the finance ministry said in a November Economic Bulletin released on Friday.

"Although total output grew only 1.5 percent in the first six months of 1996 ... the strong third quarter, combined with an apparently favourable trend for the remainder of the year, will probably raise the average growth rate for the year close to the 2.8 percent predicted in late summer," it said.
Finland is on target to meet in 1997 the criteria to join Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) from the start in 1999, the ministry added.
"Government debt as defined by the requirements for EMU will be slightly below 60 percent of GDP both this year and next," it said in the statement.
"The total public finance deficit is expected to be about three percent of GDP this year and will fall even lower next year," it added.
Its September forecast put the public debt to GDP ratio at 61.8 percent in 1996 and at 61.0 percent in 1997, and the deficit at 2.9 percent in 1996 and at 1.4 percent in 1997.
Finnish inflation, among the lowest in Europe for the past few years, will nudge up, but the ministry said "no significant cost or price pressures are in view after the new year".
The EMU criterion on inflation says inflation growth in 1997 must not exceed by more than 1.5 percentage points the rates of inflation in the three EU member states with the lowest inflation.
The finance ministry's September inflation forecast was 0.8 percent this year and 1.5 percent in 1997.
Finland on October 14 linked the markka to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) to ensure it would meet the EMU criterion on currency stability.
